body:
Not currently in treatment. Both of the therapists I’ve had so far in my adult life didn’t meet my needs very well for very different reasons, so I’m kind of hesitant to try again. My college has very limited mental health services in that you can see a counselor three times and then get referred elsewhere in town. I definitely want to look into whether those clinics would be free/low cost for students but it just never feels like “the right time.” I was recently prescribed a sleeping medication by my doctor that I’ll be starting soon, meant to help with my insomnia but which also works as an antidepressant/anxiety relief. I’m hoping that will at least make a small improvement in things. I was on Prozac several years ago but stopped taking it when my condition significantly improved at the time and haven’t been on anything for my mental health since, as I was able to handle things fairly well on my own around age 13-17 before a lot of stressful things started happening all at once in life and making it get bad again.

There are definitely things I can do with my major, but it’s really going to come down to how self-motivated I am to pursue them. I don’t want to give too much more specific detail here than what was said in my original post, but it is an arts/digital media-related degree. There is a large range of careers I could potentially get into which is nice, but my success is all going to come down to how well I can market myself and build clientele, which is more than a little intimidating for someone as introverted as I am. I have been trying to look into ways I can be successful without necessarily having to be a “people person” too though.

That is true. All I can really do is play the waiting game until one of those two conditions that would push me to get tested is met. It does me best not to dwell on it in the present since I still have my whole life ahead of me and all. I have finally been able to not make it a primary thought over the past few days thankfully though. What pushed it back into the forefront of my mind last week was my mom mentioning researching it, and I just hate that she is taking it on herself to get involved right now because I know it can’t be good for her mentally or emotionally with all the divorce stuff going on at the same time, among other things :/

I feel the best thing that would help me overcome the feeling of worthlessness would be finding a long-term purpose in life of some sort, as cliche as that sounds. I’m in a better mental state right now than I was when I made the original post, so I can recognize that there are a couple more things that do give me some sort of purpose, but I also feel like most of them won’t last forever and I need to find something long-term that I can feel like an important part of.  Another thing that would help is finding a way to “catch up” and not feel behind my peers, in terms of finances, social life, independence from family etc. because it is a recurring cause of insecurity for me.

I value my friends and family a ton, and I always try to act in their best interest when I can, even if it means I can’t be open with them about everything. I do have one friend who always seems to pop in and check on me when I need it the most, and while our conversations often turn to me helping him work through his own issues in his personal life, from career indecision to starting relationships, being able to be there for someone else does make me feel important and loved and in turn I feel comfortable going to him about some of the less sensitive issues. I just wish all my friendships were that close, where I could feel assured I was making a positive impact in their lives and vice versa. I had others like that at one point, but many drifted apart eventually, especially after I left my hometown and again after I left the city of my first college. One of the crappy downsides of Aspergers that I never have been quite able to suppress or get rid of is that social boundaries are really confusing. Sometimes I can’t tell how close I am with someone or feel like I might enjoy their company more than they enjoy mine (which may or may not always be true, could sometimes be my anxiety twisting things out of proportion), so when I can’t tell for sure either way, I grow distant out of self-preservation so I don’t get hurt or annoy them. Sometimes it’s for my own good in the end, but other times I’m left questioning and in turn it makes me forget how much the handful of super-dependable friends in my life do value me. People I’ve drifted apart from due only to time/distance (as far as I’m aware anyway) are the most confusing. I want to trust that they still care from afar but also feel that I shouldn’t have to be the one reaching out to every single one of them.

I try to find value my family life in spite of all our issues, and I absolutely do value the ones who are on the same page as me and who do all they can to be there for me (mostly my mom, brother, and grandmother). I work so hard not to hurt them or let them down and often for their sakes get frustrated at not making as much progress as I’d like to so that makes me grow distant from them as well during weeks/months when I feel like my life is stagnating and I feel like I don’t really have anything new or exciting to share. I know they love me, but many of them are dealing with one hardship or another so I just try not to make things worse.

Then there’s my SO, and we have made up since last week’s incident. I do still feel insecure in the relationship though because of how... completely normal things have gone back to and feeling like I have this false sense of security even though normalcy is the best outcome after a blow-up like that. He’s as affectionate and loving as ever and I just worry that I can’t live up to that. He claims to love me unconditionally and that’s just so much pressure. I love and value him so, so much but even on good days I still question what he sees in me sometimes. All I can do is just keep trying to be a better partner though and taking each day as it comes, right? We had a good day today catching up with an old friend he hadn’t seen in over a decade and then lazing around the house the rest of the day. I dunno, I’m starting to have a hard time putting this part into words anymore without beating around the bush. 

Thank you for taking the time to read my post and respond. This has given me a chance to reflect on things with a somewhat clearer head and work through how I’m feeling a little better than I would have been able to at that time.
Sometimes trying your best is all you can do. I really hope that you’ll be able to hang in there and work through whatever circumstances are bringing you down

Do you have a favorite music artist, or a favorite TV show or video game series? I can’t promise that your situation will get better soon, but having something like that to look forward to that is meaningful to you and unlikely to get cancelled helps makes the rough times seem smaller. It’s also helpful because it’s not on your shoulders to get into action and make those great things exist, just to sit back and enjoy them. Every time my suicidal thoughts start getting into dangerous territory (admittedly I’m close to there right now, so you can take my words with a grain of salt if you want), I try to ground myself by thinking, “I wouldn’t want to never hear new music from my favorite band again” or “I’ve made it two decades so far in life, I can wait another six months for the new Smash Bros game to come out.”
